content: Traditional programming explicitly encodes rules, while machine learning learns patterns or parameters from examples to make predictions or decisions.
interview_relevance: Explain supervised learning at a high level.

content: Training adjusts model parameters using data; inference uses an already trained model to produce outputs for new inputs.
Overfitting occurs when a model fits training data too closely and generalizes poorly to unseen data.
Precision measures the fraction of predicted positives that are correct, while recall measures the fraction of actual positives that are found.
interview_relevance: Choose metrics based on error costs.

content: An embedding represents text or another object as a numerical vector so semantic relationships can be compared computationally.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves relevant external context and supplies it to a generative model before producing an answer.
interview_relevance: Explain ingestion, retrieval, context, and generation.

content: Vector similarity compares embeddings using measures such as cosine similarity to find semantically related items.
interview_relevance: Explain why semantic retrieval differs from keyword search.

content: An LLM hallucination is an unsupported or incorrect generated statement. Retrieval, grounding, constrained prompts, and verification can reduce but not eliminate this risk.
